area: testbed hardening: enforce the declared mechanics contract instead of only declaring it

find.report_claim: cycle 150 declared mechanics.core = [shooter/sim.py, shooter/bot.py] and a mechanics.test command so an agent could find the headless AI-testable core from configuration alone
find.live_evidence: nothing enforced that the declared files stay headless: a future import of keystone.gpu, a wall-clock read, an unseeded random.Random() or a core-to-presentation import would break the promise silently while project.json kept claiming it
find.consumer_evidence: the contract is the only machine-readable statement that the mechanics core runs without a GL context, so its accuracy is what lets an agent trust it instead of reading 543 tests

read: shooter/sim.py and shooter/bot.py import graphs and RNG construction sites
killed: replacing random.Random with keystone.rng.RandomStream: SplitMix64 draws a different sequence, so every recorded bot campaign, fairness figure and evidence hash would change -- a behaviour change disguised as a portability cleanup
asserting the properties by grepping source text: an import inside a function or a differently-spelled call would slip through
banning 'time' as a name: sim.py legitimately has a self.time field, so the check must look at imported modules and attribute calls, not identifiers
analyze.survivor: parse the AST of the declared core and assert no GL/app/web/presentation imports, no clock or entropy modules, no unseeded RNG construction, a one-way dependency with the presentation layer, and a working headless seeded run

fix.shooter: tests/test_mechanics_contract.py (6 tests) validates the contract shape and that the test command names existing files, forbids GL/app/web/presentation imports in the core, forbids time/datetime/secrets/multiprocessing plus clock and entropy names, requires every random.Random construction in the core to be explicitly seeded and forbids SystemRandom, proves two Seed-7 Sim instances agree after 300 headless steps, and asserts the dependency direction (game may import the core; the core may import no shooter module). The suite is added to mechanics.test and to the README tree

shooter.mutation: inserting 'import time' into sim.py failed only the wall-clock test; removing the seed from one random.Random() call failed only the seeded-RNG test; pointing mechanics.test at tests/test_does_not_exist.py failed only the well-formed-contract test; sim.py and project.json were each restored byte-identically (sha256 match)
shooter.gates: 5/5 (hygiene, guidelines, secrets, test, mechanics); the mechanics gate now includes the contract suite
